reason: E3 directly supports the premise that edge dislocations govern strength in specific refractory BCC HEAs (NbTaTiV, CrMoNbV). E1 speculates on edge dislocation mechanisms for strength retention but does not confirm dominance. E2 discusses screw dislocation core structure and ductility, not edge dislocation dominance or friction. No cited evidence supports the claims that specific processing can increase edge dislocation fraction or that edge dislocations inherently experience higher lattice friction in these alloys.
premises: In refractory BCC HEAs, edge dislocations can dominate plastic flow, contrary to conventional BCC alloys where screw dislocations govern.
Severe plastic deformation plus tailored annealing can increase the relative fraction of edge dislocations in these alloys.
Edge dislocations experience higher lattice friction in these alloys due to severe lattice distortion.
A higher fraction of edge dislocations leads to increased hardness and yield strength.
